topic: Japanese clinical/pathological personality trait normative data
scope_note: General-population pathology-side proxies for HEXACO-based checklist. Severe-illness epidemiology is reference only.

sources.title: 日本版 Personality Inventory for DSM-5 短縮版 (PID-5-BF-J) の開発及び信頼性・妥当性の検討
sources.authors: Horie K., Shichita C., Kuroki T.
sources.journal: 九州大学総合臨床心理研究 (Bulletin of Center for Clinical Psychology and Human Development, Kyushu University)

instrument.name: PID-5-BF-J
instrument.scale: 0-3 (4-point: 非常に当てはまらない/ほとんどしない … 非常に当てはまる/よくそうする)
instrument.translation_method: Forward translation by 1 psychiatrist + 2 clinical psychology researchers; back-translation; confirmed with original author Krueger

cfa_fit.note: 適合度は十分とは言えず

limitations: Antagonism α=.49 (low) — single-item-cluster issue, not generalizable to community/clinical
CFA fit inadequate — factor structure not fully replicated
sources.usefulness_for_checklist: Best available Japanese PID-5 reference. Domain Ms cluster around 1.0 on the 0-3 scale; SDs ~0.5. Useful as soft cutoff: domain mean > 1.5 (~1 SD above) suggests salient pathology-side trait. Antagonism reliability too poor to use single-domain — combine with HEXACO low-H+low-A instead.

sources.title: 日本語版 Short Dark Triad (SD3-J) の作成
sources.journal: パーソナリティ研究 (Japanese Journal of Personality)
sources.usefulness_for_checklist: Best Japanese subclinical psychopathy/Machiavellianism reference. Note Mach M=3.53 on 1-5 scale is HIGH for student sample (above midpoint) — Japanese baseline is not low. Use SD3-J Ms as anchors when flagging dark traits via HEXACO low-H.

sources.title: 日本語版 Dark Triad Dirty Dozen (DTDD-J) 作成の試み
sources.authors: Tamura A., Oshio A., Tanaka K., Masui K., Jonason P.K.
sources.sex_difference: Male > Female significant on Psychopathy and Narcissism; Mach n.s.

sources.type: Normal-range Big Five Japanese norm (reference axis)
sources.title: A validation of the Japanese adaptation of the Big Five Inventory-2
sources.authors: Yoshino S., Shimotsukasa T., Oshio A., Hashimoto Y., Ueno Y., Mieda T., Migiwa I., Sato T., Kawamoto S., Soto C.J., John O.P.
sources.usefulness: Use as Japanese community baseline for normal-range traits. Note Japanese Agreeableness M=3.26 (50th percentile), Negative Emotionality M=3.06 (slightly above midpoint — Japanese sample is on average mildly elevated on neuroticism vs Western samples).

winsberg2019_global_meta.title: The prevalence of personality disorders in the community: a global systematic review and meta-analysis
winsberg2019_global_meta.authors: Volkert J., Gablonski T.C., Rabung S.
winsberg2019_global_meta.asia_note: No Asia subgroup; HIC vs LMIC only. Four of five comparative studies found lower PD prevalence in Asian samples (Huang et al. 2014 review).

wmh_japan_kawakami2016.title: Lifetime and 12-month prevalence ... World Mental Health Japan Survey
wmh_japan_kawakami2016.note: Did NOT assess personality disorders. Reports anxiety 12mo 4.9%, mood 2.3%, impulse control 0.7%, substance 1.0%. Sample N=4130 community. Useful only as comorbidity reference.
wmh_japan_kawakami2016.limitation: No Japanese national survey of DSM-5 PD prevalence exists as of 2026-05.

japanese_clinical_observation_moriya1993.title: Diagnosis and clinical features of BPD in the East and West
japanese_clinical_observation_moriya1993.note: Female outpatient (Japan, 18-30, N=85): 38% met BPD criteria via Diagnostic Interview for Borderlines. Strictly clinical sample — not community prevalence.

kato2012_adolescent_suicide.title: Frequency and clinical features of BPD in adolescent suicide attempts in Japan
kato2012_adolescent_suicide.authors: Kato K., Mikami K., Nishino R., et al.
kato2012_adolescent_suicide.note: Adolescent serious suicide attempters had higher BPD diagnosis rate than adult attempters (χ2=4.42, p<.05); especially female adolescents. Sub-clinical proxy: emotional instability + interpersonal conflict in young women.

hexaco_dark_triad_link.key_finding: Honesty-Humility ↔ Dark Triad correlations approach convergent-validity levels (especially with Machiavellianism). Low-H + Low-A profile captures Cluster B traits (NPD/ASPD axis) without clinical instrument.
hexaco_dark_triad_link.japanese_note: Japanese HEXACO-PI psychometric properties confirmed (Lee & Ashton, 2007; sample N~679 students). No published Japanese community norm for H-H means/SDs found in this search — pending check.
hexaco_dark_triad_link.application_for_checklist: Recommended composite: low Honesty-Humility (Modesty, Greed-Avoidance facets) + low Agreeableness (Gentleness, Forgiveness facets) ≈ Antagonism domain of PID-5. Cross-validate by spot-checking PID-5-BF-J Antagonism items (#22 自分の欲しいものを得るために人を使う / #25 他人を騙すことは私にとって簡単なことである) against target's behavior.

checklist_design_implications: PID-5-BF-J Japanese-student baseline domain Ms are all ~1.0 on 0-3 scale (SD ~0.5). +1 SD = ~1.5, +2 SD = ~2.0. Use 1.5 as 'noticeably elevated', 2.0 as 'concerning'.
Antagonism (PID-5) is poorly measured by short forms in Japan (α=.49). For Cluster-B proxy, prefer HEXACO low-H + low-A composite, sanity-checked with SD3-J Machiavellianism items.
Japanese sample shows Mach M=3.53/5 (above midpoint) — do NOT assume Japanese baseline is low. Cultural collectivism does not protect against strategic interpersonal calculation.
Sex differences (SD3-J): males higher Mach (d=-0.36) and Psychopathy (d=-0.41). Narcissism no sex diff. Apply mild sex correction.

No reliable Japanese community-prevalence numbers for BPD/NPD/ASPD. Cite global meta (~7.8% any PD, Cluster B ~2.8%) as soft prior, then weight down ~30% for Asia subgroup tendency. Avoid quoting Japanese-specific numbers — none exist.
Negative Emotionality (BFI-2-J community M=3.06/5) is slightly above scale midpoint — Japanese baseline anxiety/worry is normatively elevated vs Western. Do not over-flag this dimension.
gaps_to_note: No Japanese community PID-5 (220-item full) validation as of 2026-05; only PID-5-BF-J student sample.
No Japanese national epidemiologic survey of DSM-5 personality disorders. WMH-Japan excluded PD.
No published age/sex-stratified PID-5-BF-J norms (single 20yo student cohort).
Antagonism domain in PID-5-BF-J has unstable α — treat with caution.
MMPI-3 Japanese version: no recent open-access validation found in this search.
